summary.title: Xamarin Tutorial (Part 1): Create a Blank App
summary.one_liner: You learn what Xamarin is, how to set up Visual Studio 2015 for cross-platform mobile work, how to create a blank Xamarin.Forms app, and how the Shared and PCL code-sharing strategies differ.
keywords: shared project vs portable class library
connect visual studio to mac for ios build
how to share code across ios android windows
takeaways: Xamarin.Forms lets you build native iOS, Android and Windows UIs from shared C# code, with platform-specific code still in C# when needed.
Creating a blank Xamarin.Forms app in Visual Studio 2015 with a Shared Project strategy generates iOS, Android, UWP and shared projects.
Shared projects compile files into each platform project, while Portable Class Libraries are compiled separately and limited to a subset of .NET.
Building iOS apps from Windows requires a networked Mac with Xcode and Xamarin.iOS, connected through Remote Login, or the Visual Studio iOS Simulator add-in to debug on the PC.
summary.summary: The article is Part 1 of a Xamarin tutorial series that builds a starter cross-platform solution. It explains what Xamarin and Xamarin.Forms are, walks through installing the Cross Platform Mobile Development features in Visual Studio 2015 on Windows 10, and creates a Blank App with a Shared Project. It then covers the Shared versus Portable Class Library (PCL) strategies, pairing a Mac for iOS builds via Remote Login, and running the iOS app with the Visual Studio iOS Simulator. The author says the next part covers MVVM using the MVVM Light Toolkit.
